_about: PRO batch 14: era 1 (last scene) and era 2, Settled In (26-29).

scenarios.title: The Rookie Who Calls Home Crying
scenarios.text: A rookie in your class calls home after every practice, in the parking lot, sometimes in tears. The veterans have started to notice, and one of them has started doing an impression.

choices.label: Sit with him at lunch
choices.result: Lunch together, every day. He calls home a little less and laughs a little more, and by November he's doing impressions of the veteran.

choices.label: Ask the veterans to ease up
choices.result: The veterans, asked quietly to ease up. One of them tells you about his own first year, when he called home every night too.

choices.label: Let him find his way
choices.result: He'll find his way, you decide, and you mind your own business. He makes it through, barely, and never quite trusts the room.

scenarios.title: Don't Talk About It
scenarios.text: The specialists have a superstition: nobody says the streak out loud. A rookie just said it, at lunch, loudly.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.result: You laugh and tell the rookie it's fine. The room relaxes, and the streak goes on.

choices.label: Change nothing
choices.result: You keep every part of your routine exactly the same, including the socks.

choices.label: Make the rookie buy lunch
choices.result: You make the rookie buy the specialists lunch as penance. It becomes a tradition.

scenarios.title: The Coach for Hire
scenarios.text: A private coach who rebuilt three pro kickers offers you his offseason, for a price.

choices.label: Hire him
choices.result: You hire him for the summer. His drills are brutal and brilliant, and your leg feels new by August.

choices.label: Train with the club's staff
choices.result: You stay with the club's staff, who know your body. It's less glamorous and steady.

choices.label: Take the summer off
choices.result: You take the summer mostly off. You come back rested and a little rusty.

choices.label: Check his record first
choices.result: You call two of his former clients before deciding. Both rave. You hire him with your eyes open.

scenarios.title: The Incentive Clause
scenarios.text: Your contract pays a bonus if you hit 90 percent this season, and your agent keeps texting you the math.

choices.label: Ask your agent to stop
choices.result: You ask your agent to stop sending the math. You'll know at the end of the season.

choices.label: Chase it
choices.result: You put the number on your locker and chase it every practice.

choices.label: Forget about it
choices.result: You forget about it entirely. If it comes, it comes.

scenarios.title: The Kicker Brought In
scenarios.text: The club signs a kicker with a bigger leg and a lower salary, and puts him at the locker next to yours.

choices.label: Out-prepare him
choices.result: You out-prepare him every single day. He has the leg; you have the habits.

choices.label: Get to know him
choices.result: You get to know him. He's nervous and decent, and you both kick better without the tension.

choices.label: Ask {coach} the plan
choices.result: You ask {coach} straight out what the plan is. The answer is honest: it's open.

scenarios.title: The Bad Week
scenarios.text: You snapped at {holder}, ignored {coach} and skipped the team meal. It's been that kind of week.

choices.label: Apologize to {holder}
choices.result: You apologize to {holder} before practice. The holds are better that afternoon.

choices.label: Tell {coach} what's going on
choices.result: You tell {coach} what's actually going on. The coach listens and gives you a lighter week.

choices.label: Take a night off
choices.result: You take a night completely off: no film, no phone. It resets you.

scenarios.title: Contract Year: The Payday
scenarios.text: This is the contract that sets up your family for life, if you earn it this season.

choices.label: Make the season undeniable
choices.result: You make every practice count. Nothing about this season will be an accident.

choices.label: Let your agent work
choices.result: You let your agent handle every conversation and keep your head on kicking.

choices.label: Talk it through at home
choices.result: You talk it through with your family. Their calm becomes your calm.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Discount
scenarios.text: The club offers less than the market and asks you to take it because you're family here.

choices.label: Take the discount
choices.result: You accept the discount. The club remembers, and so does the locker room.

choices.label: Meet in the middle
choices.result: You ask your agent to find the middle. It takes two weeks, and everyone is a little unhappy and fine.

choices.label: Test the market
choices.result: You decide to test the market next spring and kick like it all year.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Traded Away
scenarios.text: The club traded your holder's best friend at midnight. He found out from his phone.

choices.label: Check on {holder}
choices.result: You check on {holder} first thing in the morning and stay through lunch.

choices.label: Talk to the team
choices.result: You say something to the specialists about how the business works. It helps the young ones.

choices.label: Keep your head down
choices.result: You keep your head down. It's the business, and you know it could be you.

scenarios.title: {parent}'s House
scenarios.text: You could pay off {parent}'s mortgage this week with one transfer. He's told you not to, twice, in the voice he used when you were twelve.

choices.label: Do it anyway
choices.result: You pay it off and tell him after. He's furious for an hour and doesn't speak at dinner. A month later, he still has the letter from the bank on his fridge.

choices.label: Ask what he'd accept
choices.result: You ask {parent} what he would actually accept. He agrees to a loan with no interest, insists on paying it back, and pays it back early.

choices.label: Respect his wish
choices.result: You respect his wish and let it go. He's proud of that, in his quiet way, and you send money to his church instead.

choices.label: Do it the way that worked before
choices.result: You set it up the way you did last time: quietly, through the bank, with his name on everything. He grumbles and signs.
choices.lock_text: having helped your family with money before

scenarios.title: First Day of School
scenarios.text: Your kid's first day of school is a Thursday practice.

choices.label: Ask to come in late
choices.result: You ask {coach} to come in an hour late. You're there for the first wave goodbye.

choices.label: Go to practice
choices.result: You go to practice and get a video. You watch it four times at lunch.

choices.label: Plan around it
choices.result: You plan the morning with the coach and your partner. You make the drop-off and the meeting.

scenarios.title: {parent} Is Getting Older
scenarios.text: {parent} forgets the name of a neighbor he's known for twenty years.

choices.label: Go home for a weekend
choices.result: You go home for the bye weekend and spend every minute with him.

choices.label: Find him a doctor
choices.result: You find him a specialist and go to the first appointment by video.

choices.label: Call more often
choices.result: You start calling every other day. It's not much, and it's something.

scenarios.title: {sibling}'s Own Shot
scenarios.text: {sibling} has a tryout of his own, and he wants you there.

choices.label: Be there
choices.result: You fly in for the tryout and stand behind the fence. He looks for you before every kick.

choices.label: Coach him by phone
choices.result: You coach him by phone the night before: one thought, one routine.

choices.label: Send a message
choices.result: You send a message and watch the video later. He understands, mostly.

choices.label: Tell him what you learned
choices.result: You tell {sibling} the hardest thing you ever learned: show up, tell the truth, let the rest go. Then you're there at the fence.
choices.lock_text: having learned what showing up means
